    AI Overview
    As of April 2026, the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) is temporarily suspending employer contributions to the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS) to conserve cash amid a severe financial crisis, threatening to run out of funds within 12 months. The move, effective April 10, aims to save approximately
    billion through September 30 by pausing
    million in biweekly payments, but officials state there is no immediate impact on current or future retirees. 
    Key Details of the Pension Suspension 
    • Action Taken: USPS is halting its employer contributions to the FERS defined benefit plan.
    • Continued Payments: USPS will continue to transmit employee contributions to FERS, as well as contributions to the Thrift Savings Plan (TSP) and Social Security.
    • Financial Context: The agency reported
      billion in net losses since 2007, with quarterly losses reaching
      billion in early 2026.
    • Past Precedent: The Postal Service previously suspended these payments in 2011 during a similar financial crisis. 
    Postal Retirement System Background 
    • Plan Types: Career employees are covered under FERS or the older Civil Service Retirement System (CSRS).
    • Funding Mechanism: Unlike other federal agencies that receive appropriations, USPS must fund its retirement obligations through its own operating revenue.
    • Unfunded Liabilities: All three retirement-related funds (including health benefits) have unfunded liabilities. 
    For more context on the historical challenges of these funds, see this USPS OIG report. For details on the 2026 suspension, see this NewsNation article.

    How many years do you have to work at the post office to get a pension?
    If you leave with 30 years or more of service, then you be will eligible for an unreduced retirement benefit when you reach your MRA (age 55-57).

    How much is the average postal workers pension?
    As an example of USPS retirement under CSRS, a postal worker with a high-3 average of around $60,000 and 20 years of service earns $1,824 a month without any deductions. That equals about $22,000 annually. A worker with the same salary and 40 years of service earns $3,837 monthly, or about $46,000 annually.

    How much is a post office pension per month?
    The amount of money a postal worker makes in retirement depends on their age and how long they worked as a postal worker or government employee. A postal worker who retired in 2023 with 25 years of service would make a monthly basic annuity between $1,447-$1,478.Nov 3, 2023
